title: Civil Claims for Negligence Arising from Safety Breaches during SAF Training
what_it_is: Civil Claims for Negligence Arising from Safety Breaches during SAF Training

sections.label: Amending GPA section 14
sections.summary: Proposes amending section 14 of the GPA to allow civil liability in negligence for Armed Forces or Government deaths or injuries during training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Specifically, I would like to propose that section 14 of the GPA should be amended to allow civil liability in the tort of negligence in respect of a member of the Armed Forces or the Government for death or personal injury during training as a result of any conduct by any officer during training that conspicuously violates safety protocols, procedures and regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: An example would be if an officer or instructor fails to comply with Training Safety Regulations (TSR) or any training safety protocols recommended in any Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) lesson plans or manuals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: There should be a clear distinction between training and operations for purposes of liability under section 14 of GPA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In March 2016, I filed a Parliamentary Question to the Minister for Defence on issues relating to the death of Private (Pte) Dominique Sarron Lee during SAF training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I asked a supplementary question as to whether the Government would consider amending section 14 of GPA to allow certain situations of liability instead of the current absolute exemption from liability for all claims attributable to service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I gave a few examples for consideration: the waiver can be limited to actual operations and should not apply to training, or when a death or personal injury occurred as a result of omission from observing TSRs or when the negligence of an officer has some causal connection with the death or personal injury.

sections.label: Pte Lee death safety revision
sections.summary: Pte Dominique Sarron Lee's death led to revised safety procedures for smoke grenades in training, including a change in grenade type.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The tragic death of Pte Dominique Sarron Lee brought a revision to safety procedures relating to the use of smoke grenades in training, including a change to the type of smoke grenade SAF uses.

sections.label: Civil liability for safety breaches
sections.summary: Training accidents from clear or deliberate breaches of safety codes by officers should have channels for civil liability, as criminal liability exists.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: When a training accident occurs because of clear, and especially deliberate breaches of established safety codes by officers responsible for conducting the training or recklessness as to its compliance, there should be channels for civil liability, just as there are channels for criminal liability.

sections.label: Amend GPA section 14
sections.summary: Section 14 of the GPA should be amended to reflect this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Section 14 of GPA should be amended to reflect this.

sections.label: Civil suits reduce moral hazard
sections.summary: Knowledge of the possibility of a civil suit reduces moral hazard by making the gravity of consequences more evident.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Knowledge of the possibility of a civil suit reduces the moral hazard by making the gravity of consequences more evident.

sections.label: Limited civil liability circumstances
sections.summary: Civil liability should be allowed for limited circumstances, such as when officers have clearly failed to comply with TSRs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, I have said today that civil liability should be allowed for limited circumstances, for instance, when officers have clearly failed to comply with TSRs.

sections.label: MINDEF compensation offer rejected
sections.summary: MINDEF offered compensation to Pte Lee's family, which was rejected, and said amounts are not disclosed but are generally two to four times WICA amounts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: MINDEF mentioned in their press release of 7 March 2016 of an offer of compensation to Pte Lee's family which was rejected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: MINDEF also said that "To respect privacy and maintain confidentiality, compensation amounts are not disclosed, but are generally two to four times that of amounts provided under the Work Injury Compensation Act" (WICA).

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It is not very clear what was offered to the family but, for avoidance of doubt, the awards under WICA are usually less than awards under common law negligence claims.

sections.label: Settlement subject to MINDEF discretion
sections.summary: Settlement is subject to MINDEF's discretion, and allowing legal scrutiny would build public confidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Furthermore, such settlement will be subject to the discretion of MINDEF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: If the law were to allow civil liability and MINDEF would still like to make a "without prejudice" offer during negotiations for future claims, it may well be looked upon quite differently by claimants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: This willingness to allow for legal scrutiny builds public confidence.

sections.label: Judicial oversight encourages safety protocols
sections.summary: Allowing independent judicial oversight through civil proceedings encourages SAF commanders to be mindful of safety protocols in training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Declaring values and laying out safety regulations are but one step towards greater safety for our troops during training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: And by allowing independent judicial oversight through civil proceedings when there are violations of safety standards, SAF further encourages commanders to be mindful of safety protocols in the controlled environments that training is supposed to be.

sections.label: Amend GPA for civil liability
sections.summary: The GPA should be amended to allow civil liability in negligence against the Armed Forces or Government for death or personal injury from conduct conspicuously violating safety protocols during training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: We owe it to our citizens and our women and men in uniform.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: I believe that the GPA should be amended to allow civil liability in negligence against a member of the Armed Forces or the Government for causing death or personal injury during training as a result of any conduct in training that conspicuously violates safety protocols, procedures and regulations.

sections.label: Coroner found TSR infractions not cause
sections.summary: The coroner found the TSR infractions were associated but not the direct cause of death.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The facts are established and the Member failed to mention that, in this particular case that he referred to, the coroner made a finding on the cause of death, and while the infractions in the TSRs were associated, they were not the direct cause of death.

sections.label: SAF servicemen jailed and fined
sections.summary: SAF servicemen have been jailed and fined as a consequence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: SAF Servicemen have, indeed, been jailed and fined as a consequence.

sections.label: Compensation under SAF Pensions regulations
sections.summary: JC Kannan explained that section 14 removed the Plaintiff's tort right of action but the Plaintiff is entitled to compensation under SAF Pensions regulations, about two to four times Workmen's Compensation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: JC Kannan also explained that while section 14 removed the Plaintiff's right of action in tort, the Plaintiff is nevertheless entitled to compensation under the SAF Pensions regulations and our compensation, as I have previously said in this House, is about two to four times of the Workmen's Compensation.

sections.label: UK military protection removed 1987
sections.summary: The UK removed this protection for their military in 1987.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The UK removed this protection for their military in 1987.

sections.label: Section 14 commander training confidence
sections.summary: Retired British commanders reported the removal undermined personnel's willingness to accept responsibility and take risks, affecting operational effectiveness; section 14 gives commanders confidence to train realistically.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Retired senior British commanders also reported that it had undermined armed forces personnel's willingness to accept responsibility and take necessary risks, with the consequent impact on operational effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: I will give a simple example: training for the Individual Physical Proficiency Test (IPPT).

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The TSR says you do it; you keep within the TSR.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: But if you push someone to run faster than he can and he collapses, and it is found that he had an undetected condition after the fact, and if the person, the commander or even the fellow Servicemen feel that he can be sued, not protected, how many commanders do you think will encourage their unit to train harder?

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: This is a reality we face; there are inherent risks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: I think we have struck a good balance between maintaining very high safety standards, and  section 14 provides us that confidence for our commanders to train realistically.
